newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Polish central bank head sees inflation on target.
newsitem.headline: Polish central bank head sees inflation on target.

text.p: Polish central bank chief Hanna Gronkiewicz-Waltz said on Friday she was confident Poland's 1997 inflation rate would come in on target at 13 percent but warned interest rates would have to rise.

"Our target is the inflation rate at the forecast 13 percent," she told Reuters Financial Television in an interview at the Second Central and Eastern European Economic Summit here. "I think that for the first time we can get 13 percent."

Gronkiewicz-Waltz said the economic costs of major flooding in Poland over the past few days may affect spending and inflation targets this year. But she said she could not estimate the exact magnitude of such effects.
The central bank chief said she remained worried about strong credit growth and warned that interest rates would have to rise further to dampen the strong expansion of money supply.
"We have to tighten our monetary policy because we have very high credit growth. Our interest rates must be adjusted to money supply," she said.
Gronkiewicz-Waltz also said she was unhappy with the government's budget deficit target of 2.8 percent of gross domestic product this year.
"It really should be lower than last year's 2.5 percent, but I'm afraid we had an election year and that had an effect on consumption spending," she said.
"In this situation, with quite a high growth rate at 5.5 percent, the budget deficit should be constrained," she added.
Gronkiewicz-Waltz said the zloty currency, subject to a crawling peg, still had some room for devaluation this year.
"According to the budget, the devaluation rate this year should be nine percent," she said. "We didn't reduce it in practice, so we have some room."
